agnostic_oa_scheme_invariant_recursive_s.boundary_or_failure: The finiteness claim is demonstrated in a renormalization toy model and presupposes that bracket evaluation leaves the designated divergent part unchanged. The unit does not define a general class of projections for which the argument works, nor does it establish the analytic or physical validity of arbitrary evaluation schemes.
agnostic_oa_scheme_invariant_recursive_s.interpretation: Source fact: cuts induce nested bracket evaluations, the antipode supplies signed counterterms, and full cuts pair with normal cuts so that each contribution becomes X minus its bracket evaluation; preserving the divergent part makes that difference finite. Inference: the combinatorial correction rule and the evaluation scheme are separate layers, so invariance across schemes comes from a preservation contract rather than from identical evaluations.
agnostic_oa_scheme_invariant_recursive_s.nonparaphrase_operation: Identify an obstructing component and choose an evaluator P that preserves exactly that component. Generate recursive corrections from the decomposition antipode, retain where P is applied as bracket structure, and pair each unprojected contribution X with its projected counterpart P(X). The residual X-P(X) removes the obstruction while allowing scheme-dependent finite information to vary.
agnostic_oa_scheme_invariant_recursive_s.source_support: The unit identifies subdivergent sectors with admissible cuts and forests with arbitrary cuts, derives bracketed counterterms from the antipode, and states that any bracket evaluation preserving the divergent part is a valid scheme. It then explains finiteness by pairing full and normal cuts into differences X-[X].
agnostic_oa_scheme_invariant_recursive_s.uncertainty: The structural cancellation argument is explicit, but the unit checks typical schemes only informally and does not supply a general analytic proof. The abstraction from divergent-part extraction to an arbitrary obstruction-preserving evaluator is a bounded inference.

agnostic_oa_tree_dependency_encoding.boundary_or_failure: A single rooted tree represents laminar dependence: subproblems are nested or disjoint. Genuine overlaps are not captured by this encoding without linear combinations, decorations, or an enlarged construction. The representation also forgets analytic values and treats the order of disjoint branches as irrelevant.
agnostic_oa_tree_dependency_encoding.interpretation: Source fact: vertices stand for integration variables, an edge toward the root denotes nesting, and vertices on separate branches denote disjoint integrations. Inference: rooted-tree shape is a quotient of the analytic problem that preserves only the dependency partial order relevant to recursive decomposition; depth records containment and branching records independent sibling structure.
agnostic_oa_tree_dependency_encoding.nonparaphrase_operation: Strip a recursively nested problem to its dependency relation: create one vertex per subproblem, connect each subproblem to its immediate container, orient toward a distinguished outer root, and place incomparable disjoint subproblems on separate branches. Perform structural reasoning on the tree, then return to analytic data only when values rather than dependency shape matter.
agnostic_oa_tree_dependency_encoding.source_support: The unit says configurations of nested or disjoint subdivergences can be described by rooted trees, assigns each vertex to an integration variable, interprets an edge toward the root as nested integration, and interprets unconnected vertices as disjoint integrations. It also defines root removal and grafting as inverse operations on the resulting tree and forest representations.
agnostic_oa_tree_dependency_encoding.uncertainty: The generic dependency interpretation is well supported by prose, but the motivating examples and some tree identities rely on damaged figures. No claim of novelty or of adequacy for non-laminar dependency systems can be established from this unit.

agnostic_oa_scheme_invariant_recursive_s.context_risk: Moderate: the toy-model cancellation argument is explicit, but typical schemes are checked only informally and the span does not prove analytic validity for a general class of evaluators.
agnostic_oa_scheme_invariant_recursive_s.faithfulness: The candidate correctly identifies bracketed counterterms, the antipode-induced normal/full cut pairing, and the condition that bracket evaluation leave the divergent part unchanged so each difference is finite.
agnostic_oa_scheme_invariant_recursive_s.missed_mechanism: It should explicitly identify the invariant conclusion as finiteness after subtraction, not the value of the renormalized finite part, which the source allows to depend on the chosen scheme.
agnostic_oa_scheme_invariant_recursive_s.paraphrase_risk: Low: pairing X with its bracket evaluation is the operative cancellation step and is more than a stylistic restatement.
agnostic_oa_scheme_invariant_recursive_s.revision_instructions: Replace invariance across schemes with scheme-robust finiteness under the stated preservation condition, and replace preserves exactly that component with leaves the designated divergent part unchanged; do not imply identical finite outputs.
agnostic_oa_scheme_invariant_recursive_s.unsupported_or_imported: The word invariance is too strong if read as equality of renormalized values, and exactly is stronger than the source's condition.
